sentences.text:
1. Heard counsel for petitioner, counsel for complainant as well as learned Public Prosecutor and perused the material available on record.
2.

Instant bail application has been filed by petitioner under Section 483 of BNSS in connection with FIR No. 7/2025 registered at Police Station- Bidasar, District- Churu for offences under Sections 376(2)(n), 506 & 354A of IPC and Sections 7/8, 11/12 of POCSO Act.

3. Counsel for petitioner states that petitioner is in custody since 20.01.2025; prosecutrix is a major and married woman of 45 years, who admits to enter into friendship/ sexual relationship with the petitioner since her husband lives outstation and has gone to Dubai to earn livelihood.

Learned counsel submits that the allegations levelled against petitioner, regarding molestation of (Uploaded on 06/12/2025 at 11:33:39 AM) [2025:RJ-JD:52335] (2 of 2) [CRLMB-5264/2025] prosecutrix's minor daughter, are vague and non-specific, therefore, in such circumstances, petitioner be released Illiyas vs State Of Rajasthan (2025:Rj-Jd:52335) on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133587898/
1 on bail.
4. Learned Public Prosecutor and counsel for complainant have opposed the bail application.
Counsel for complainant submits that the trial of present criminal case, has substantially been concluded and the sessions case is likely to be decided.

5. Having considered the rival contentions and taking into consideration the statements of prosecutrix as also her minor daughter, prima facie, relationship between petitioner and prosecutrix appears to be consensual; allegations of minor molestation with daughter of proseuctirx, are non-specific; petitioner is custody since 20.01.2025; since statements of prosecutrix and her minor daughter, have already been recorded, there is no possibility to induce/ threaten the prosecution witness/ evidence by the petitioner; petitioner does not have any criminal antecedent and is a labour class, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court deems it just and proper to release the petitioner on bail.
6.

Accordingly, the bail application is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner Illiyas S/o Mushtaq shall be released on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.
